title: Union-find: path halving, union by size
summary: Merge groups of nodes 0..n-1 and ask whether two share a group. find() halves the path as it climbs; union() hangs the smaller root under the larger and returns False when already joined. Near O(1) amortized.
triggers: groups that only ever merge, with 'are x and y connected?' queries
adding undirected edges one at a time and spotting the first cycle
prompts: Accounts that share an email address belong to the same person. After all merges, how many distinct people remain?
Cables are added between servers one at a time. Report the first cable that closes a loop.
invariant: Following parent pointers from any node reaches its group's root, and size[root] is that group's size.
mantra: Find both roots; hang the smaller under the larger.
pitfalls: Union the roots, never the raw nodes.
This is path halving (parent = grandparent), not full path compression; both give near-constant time.
Count components as n minus the successful unions.
union() returning False means the edge closes a cycle.

anchors.name: Number of Provinces
anchors.trick: Union every connected pair; provinces = n - successful unions.

anchors.name: Redundant Connection
anchors.trick: The first edge whose union returns False.

anchors.name: Accounts Merge
